data.name: Ithamar
data.gender_notes: Ithamar is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew word yatham, meaning 'given by God'. In the Bible, Ithamar was a priest and the younger brother of Zadok. The name Ithamar carries the meaning “Given by God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ithamar usually hope their child will grow to embody given by god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder of God's blessings and provision.
data.etymology: Ithamar belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Given by God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ithamar total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: אִיתָמָר
in_hebrew.meaning: אי תמר - האי של תמר, תמר שלי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אִיתָמָר הוא שם פרטי עברי שפירושו 'אי תמר' או 'תמר שלי'. השם מורכב משתי מילים: 'אי' שפירושו 'אי' או 'מקום מבודד', ו'תמר' שפירושו 'תמר' - עץ פרי פופולרי במקרא. השם אִיתָמָר מוזכר במקרא כבן של אהרון הכהן, אחיו של נדב, אביהו, אלעזר ואיתמר (שמות כה יז, ויקרא י ה, כה טז). אִיתָמָר היה אחד הכהנים בישראל ומילא תפקיד חשוב בפולחן.

in_greek.name: Ιθάμαρ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ιθάμαρ είναι ένα όνομα ελληνικό που προέρχεται από την Εβραϊκή γλώσσα. Στη Βίβλο, ο Ιθάμαρ ήταν ο τέταρτος γιος του Ααρων και της Ελσαβεέ (Έξοδος 6:23, 28:41, Λευϊτικό 10:6). Το όνομα πιθανότατα σημαίνει 'νησί της θάμνας' ή 'νησί του φοίνικα', συμβολίζοντας ένα μέρος με πλούσια βλάστηση.

in_latin.name: Ithamar
in_latin.long_meaning: Ithamar, nomen hebraicum, in latinum translatum, significat 'insulam palmae' vel 'locum tutum'. In scripturis sacris, Ithamar fuit filius Aaronis, sacerdotis hebraeorum, et frater Nadab, Abihu, Eleazaris et Ithamar (Exodus 6:23, 28:41). Nomen hoc in traditione christiana, denotat tutelam et protectionem divinam.

in_english.name: Ithamar
in_english.meaning: island of palm trees or place of security
in_english.long_meaning: The name Ithamar originates from Hebrew, meaning 'island of palm trees' or 'place of security'. It is derived from two Hebrew words: 'ay', meaning 'island' or 'place', and 'tamar', meaning 'palm tree'. In the Bible, Ithamar was the fourth son of Aaron, the high priest of Israel (Exodus 6:23, 28:41, Leviticus 10:6). The name Ithamar symbolizes protection, safety, and fertility. Throughout Christian tradition, Ithamar has been used as a given name, representing divine guidance and shelter.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ithamar has its roots in the rich cultural heritage of the ancient Hebrews. In biblical times, Ithamar was an important priestly figure who served at the tabernacle (or portable sanctuary) in the wilderness and later at the Temple in Jerusalem. This association with the sacred spaces and religious practices of the Hebrew people demonstrates the historical significance and cultural importance of the name Ithamar.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Ithamar lies in its meaning: 'given by God'. This emphasizes the idea that every life is a divine gift. In the context of biblical times, the name Ithamar held a special significance for the religious community as it highlighted the idea of God's presence and grace in their lives. Today, this name can serve as a powerful reminder of the divine origin and purpose of our lives.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ithamar is a Hebrew name meaning "abundance of the sea". It symbolizes the abundant blessings and provisions that God bestows upon His people. In Exodus, Ithamar is the name of a Levite priest who received a special portion from the sacrifices, signifying the spiritual abundance and grace bestowed upon the priesthood.

biblical_reference.note: son of Aaron, brother of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar

historical_references.reference: Ithamar was a son of Aaron and Elisheba, and was a priest in the Tabernacle during the wilderness journey of the Israelites.
Ithamar is also mentioned as the father of Ezra, who led a group of exiles back to Jerusalem in 458 BCE to rebuild the Temple.

modern_usage.modern_context: Ithamar is a biblical name of Hebrew origin, which was part of the priestly lineage of Aaron in the Tabernacle in the Old Testament. It is also a name found in many genealogies as an ancestral name. In modern literature, Ithamar is a character in various works, such as in the novel "The Red Tent" by Anita Diamant, where he is portrayed as one of Jacob's sons. Ithamar's modern usage can be found on platforms like Wikipedia, where it is detailed in religious and historical contexts, on MyHeritage, where it is a searchable name in genealogical records, and on Goodreads, where it is mentioned in connection with literary works.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Ruth Ithamar in New York, United States credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Ithamar, which means "Given by God". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
